Condom programming measures the percentage of individuals identified as being at elevated risk of HIV acquisition who received condoms through a program during the reporting period. This includes the number of people who received condoms and lubricant at least once during the reporting period. At the program/service provider level, this refers to individuals identified as being at elevated risk of HIV acquisition, including those requesting or receiving any HIV prevention intervention, individuals from key populations, and those with known risk factors or otherwise assessed as being at risk. At the population level, it involves estimating the size of each key population. 3. Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) monitoring includes the incidence of HIV infections per 100 person-years (PY) of follow-up among PrEP users. It also tracks the number of individuals receiving PrEP who test positive for HIV during the reporting period and the total PY of PrEP use during the same period. An option exists to exclude person-time on PrEP contributed by individuals who do not retest for HIV or are lost to follow-up from the denominator. 4. Adverse events related to PrEP are measured as the incidence of PrEP-related adverse events per 100 PY of follow-up. This includes the number of individuals on PrEP who experience adverse events during the reporting period and the total PY of PrEP use during the same period. Similarly, person-time contributed by individuals lost to follow-up can be excluded from the denominator. 5. Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) among PrEP users are tracked by the incidence of STI cases per 100 PY of follow-up. This includes the number of PrEP recipients identified as STI cases through syndromic or etiologic approaches during the reporting period while using PrEP, as well as the total PY of PrEP use during the same period. Again, person-time contributed by individuals lost to follow-up can be excluded from the denominator. 6. PrEP-related antiretroviral (ARV) toxicity is measured as the percentage of PrEP users who discontinued or interrupted PrEP due to serious ARV-associated toxicity during the reporting period. This includes the number of individuals who discontinued or interrupted PrEP due to toxicity and the total number of people on PrEP during the reporting period. 7. Needle-syringe programs (NSP) assess safe injecting practices among people who inject drugs. This is measured as the percentage of individuals who report using new sterile injecting equipment the last time they injected. The numerator includes survey respondents who answer yes to both questions: (1) Have you injected drugs in the past month? and (2) Did you use new sterile injecting equipment the last time you injected? 8. Opioid agonist maintenance treatment (OAMT) availability is measured as the percentage of OAMT recipients who received take-away doses during the reporting period. This includes the number of OAMT recipients who received take-away doses at least once during the reporting period and the total number of individuals receiving OAMT during the same period. 9. HIV testing services (HTS) measure the median number of days from an HIV-negative test result to the uptake of a prevention intervention. This includes the sum of the number of days from the date the test result was received to the uptake of prevention intervention for all individuals testing negative for HIV and identified as being at elevated risk for HIV acquisition. The denominator includes the number of individuals testing negative for HIV during the reporting period and identified as vulnerable to HIV acquisition, excluding those currently on PrEP and undergoing testing as part of PrEP follow-up. 10. Adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) HIV/SRH integration measures the percentage of AGYW seeking contraception or family planning services who received an HIV test. This includes the number of AGYW tested for HIV while seeking contraception or family planning services and the total number of AGYW seeking such services. 11. Co-trimoxazole (CTX) coverage measures the percentage of eligible people living with HIV who received CTX. This includes the number of people living with HIV who started CTX and the number of people newly enrolled in antiretroviral therapy (ART) who are eligible for CTX. 12. Early infant ART initiation measures the percentage of identified HIV-positive infants who initiated ART on the day of diagnosis. This includes the number of infants (under 24 months of age) started on ART on the same day as receiving an HIV-positive diagnosis during the reporting period and the total number of infants identified as HIV-positive during the same period. 13. Time to gonorrhea treatment is measured as the median number of days between the gonorrhea test date and the date treatment is prescribed or dispensed. 14. Time to treatment for pre-invasive cervical disease is measured as the median number of days between the diagnosis date of pre-invasive cervical disease and the treatment date. 15. Loss to follow-up for pre-invasive cervical disease treatment measures the proportion of women living with HIV who are lost to follow-up after receiving treatment for pre-invasive cervical disease. This includes the number of women who did not return for retesting 12 months after their treatment and the total number of women who received treatment for pre-invasive cervical disease 12 months ago. 16. HPV vaccination for women living with HIV follows either a 2-dose or 3-dose schedule. HPV vaccination is included in the WHO ART treatment card and may be based on self-report or documented vaccine delivery.
